questions.question: How do you build forms in Rails with form_with?
questions.title: Building Forms with form_with
questions.direct_answer: form_with is Rails' form builder: it generates an HTML <form> with authenticity tokens, field tags, and a route inferred from a model object. form_with model: @post builds a form for that record: f.text_field :title, f.text_area :body, f.submit. If @post is saved, it PATCHes; if new, it POSTs — form_with infers the verb and URL from the record. f.label :title, f.text_field :title, f.select :status, options — the builder f gives you typed fields. On validation failure, re-render :new and the form re-shows with @post.errors and field errors auto-highlighted. Strong params on the controller side guard the submitted fields.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know form_with model: @post builds a form, f.text_field/f.submit, and it infers POST (new) vs PATCH (saved) from the record.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Forgetting form_with needs a model: (it infers the URL/verb), or naming fields that aren't in strong params (the value is dropped).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: form_with model: @post builds a form (authenticity token, fields, route). f.text_field/f.text_area/f.submit. It infers POST (new) vs PATCH (saved) from the record.

sections.title: Rails' Form Builder
sections.content: form_with is Rails' form builder: it generates an HTML form with authenticity tokens, field tags, and a route inferred from a model object. form_with model at post builds a form for that record: f dot text_field title, f dot text_area body, f dot submit. If post is saved, it PATCHes; if new, it POSTs — form_with infers the verb and URL from the record. f dot label, f dot text_field, f dot select with options — the builder f gives you typed fields. On validation failure, re-render new and the form re-shows with post dot errors and field errors auto-highlighted. Strong params on the controller side guard the submitted fields.

sections.title: form_with Flow
sections.content:
model -> form builder f -> fields -> submit; infers POST (new) vs PATCH (saved).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[model: @post] --> F[form_with -> builder f]
  F --> Tf[f.text_field :title]
  F --> Ta[f.text_area :body]
  F --> S[f.submit]
  F --> I[infers POST/PATCH + URL]
```

sections.title: form_with
sections.content:
```ruby <%= form_with model: @post do |f| %>
<%= f.label :title %> <%= f.text_field :title %>
<%= f.label :body %> <%= f.text_area :body %>
<%= f.submit %> <% end %> ```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Forgetting form_with needs a model: (it infers the URL/verb from it).
Naming form fields not in strong params — the value is dropped on submit.
Not re-rendering :new on validation fail (redirecting loses @post + errors).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: form_with model: @post builds a form (authenticity token, fields, route).
The builder f gives typed fields: f.text_field, f.text_area, f.select, f.submit.
form_with infers the verb and URL: POST for a new record, PATCH for a saved one.
On validation failure, render :new — the form re-shows with @post.errors.
Strong params on the controller guard the submitted fields (permit only safe ones).
